items.title: Self-Host Weekly (13 November 2026)
items.body:
SPONSORED BY

Infisical

Your AI agents need access to APIs and tools. How do you secure that access? Join our Nov 18 webinar on agent identity, permissions, and secrets, plus a live Agent Vault demo. Save your spot.

Weekly Highlights

If you missed it, I posted the results of the 2026 Self-Host User Survey this week (link below). Thanks again to all who participated – in total, it received 6,221 responses (a 52% increase from last year's 4,081 🚀).

2026 Self-Host Survey Results

With so many more participants than last year, it's difficult to tell whether certain shifts reflect real trends or just a different mix of respondents. Regardless, there were a number of results I found particularly interesting:

• The number of Portainer deployments has shrunk since last year and is now neck-and-neck with Dockhand – a platform that was only released earlier this year

• Debian and Ubuntu are wildly more popular than distributions like Fedora and Arch (this year's survey marked the first appearance of this question)

• 63% of respondents avoid vibe coded apps, 25% don't mind them, and 7% avoid AI-assisted projects altogether (the rest answered 'it depends' or 'other')

• Forgejo surpassed Gitea as the most popular self-hosted Git platform

• Proton Drive (storage) usage has grown significantly since last year (it'll be interesting to see how it makes out next year given its CEO's recent headlines)

• The number of laptop deployments has now surpassed that of server clusters

• 733 respondents are still YOLO'ing their application updates

• Three people who responded to the survey are over 80 years old (hell yeah!)

And lastly, everyone's favorite app this year was – well, you'll just have to find out for yourself.

In actual news and activity:

• Home Assistant continued their bizarre product naming habits with the announcement of the Connect AUX-2, a small box designed to bring smart home capabilities to non-smart devices

• Unraid's latest v7.4.0 release finally adds container template support for multiple custom networks and fields for memory limits

• An independent developer recently launched Vacuula, a custom server implementation for Neato robot vacuums, in response to the company's decision to phase out cloud services late last year

• Evgenii Burmakin, the developer of Dawarich, has launched a Discord for self-hosted software devs – send him a DM if you'd like to join!

• Verisign, a popular domain registry, confirmed it will grandfather existing .name domains after plans to completely discontinue the TLD stirred up some backlash a few months ago

• The world was introduced to Ram Altman, a satirical bash script that sends daily emails to Sam Altman when your machine has unused RAM

Happy selfh.st/ing!

Feedback

Content Spotlight

Meet plMail, a self-hosted Gmail-style mail client. Built for users who either self-host their email or are just looking for an interface to unify multiple accounts, plMail provides a refreshing, modern take on webmail with an added emphasis on calendars via a docked side panel. Features include support for multiple account types (IMAP, Gmail, Outlook), advanced search, filter trees, optional AI features, and single sign-on.

plMail can be easily deployed via Docker and requires separate worker, database, and notification containers.
